The Minister of Defence, Maj. Gen. (retd.) Christopher Musa, has attributed the prolonged insecurity in the country partly to the inability to produce enough weapons and ammunition locally for security operations. He also stated that global conflicts had made the procurement of military equipment increasingly difficult. Musa said the country needed to strengthen its local defence industry to reduce dependence on foreign manufacturers and ensure a steady supply of weapons and equipment required to tackle insecurity. The minister spoke on Friday during the inauguration of the TETFund Centre of Excellence in Security Management, tagged the “CG Musa Security Management Hub”, at the University of Ibadan, Oyo State. He said, “Nigeria needs to begin to produce what she needs to end insecurity. Our intention is to expose our local producers to foreign and international manufacturers so that we can continue to produce what we need or what we rely on. “Why insecurity continues to be prolonged is that we do not produce all we need. Most times, when we go to buy, even with cash at hand, you can’t get them off the shelves. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “Now, with the wars going on in Ukraine, Russia and the Strait of Hormuz, it has become extremely difficult to buy even ammunition to use, not to talk of Armoured Personnel Carriers. “Since our local manufacturers are doing their best, we need to escalate to an international level.” The minister added that the security challenges confronting the country had become complex and required informed policies, credible institutions, technological innovation and a comprehensive understanding of the human dimensions of conflict. Musa emphasised the importance of collaboration between universities and defence institutions, noting that academic research could help identify the causes of insecurity and develop sustainable solutions. He said, “The academia occupies a strategic place in our national security management architecture. The battlefield may reveal the immediate manifestations of insecurity, but the university provides the intellectual environment to interrogate its causes, evaluate responses and develop sustainable solutions. We will continue to encourage collaboration between defence institutions and centres of learning to ensure that our security policies and operational approaches benefit from research, innovation and evidence-based analysis.” Musa added that the government had intensified efforts to tackle insecurity, expressing optimism that the situation was gradually improving. “We have stepped up our game in the field and are gradually improving the security situation. It is also important that everybody plays a part because it is a whole-of-nation approach. If you see something, say something,” he said. In his remarks, the Vice-Chancellor of the university, Prof. Kayode Adebowale, thanked the donor for providing a facility from which current and future generations would benefit. He said the university would ensure that the centre became an epicentre of security research in Africa. “We hope and believe that this hub serves as the nexus for multidisciplinary research and a convening ground for policymakers and academics. The facility must not become a museum of security artefacts but must be used to generate data that will guide the Ministry of Defence and our security agents,” he said. The lead researcher and technical officer at the centre, Prof. Isaac Albert, appreciated the minister for fulfilling his promise to the institution and urged him to ensure that more funds were made available for security management research and projects that would inform appropriate security policies. “It is also important for security agencies to patronise the centre and engage with its resource persons towards formulating and implementing the right security policies,” Albert said. Earlier, the Director of the TETFund Centre of Excellence in Security Management, Prof. Benjamin Aluko, urged Nigerians to enrol for the MSc and PhD programmes in Security Management at the University of Ibadan to benefit from the expertise of leading academics in the field.
